title: Internal drive unit error
shortDescription: The drive unit has detected an internal fault.
fullDescription:
Error 500 is a generic internal fault reported by the Bosch drive unit (motor). It typically indicates the controller has seen an unexpected condition, a firmware glitch, or a brief electrical irregularity.

A reboot (remove and reinsert the battery) often clears the code. If it returns, the drive unit must be diagnosed by a Bosch-certified dealer using the Bosch DiagnosticTool.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle the system
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the bike, remove the battery, wait 30 seconds, reinsert and power on.

fixSteps.title: Update firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Visit a Bosch dealer to have the drive unit firmware updated to the latest version.

fixSteps.title: Drive unit service
fixSteps.instruction: If error persists, the drive unit must be inspected or replaced by a certified dealer.

whenToCallPro: If the error persists after a power cycle, take the bike to a Bosch-certified dealer.

faq.a: Yes, but without motor assist. Resolve the error before long rides.

title: Drive unit communication fault
shortDescription: The drive unit cannot communicate with the display or battery.
fullDescription:
Error 501 indicates a communication breakdown on the CAN bus between the drive unit and other components. It is frequently caused by a loose or damaged cable at the motor or display.

Inspect all wiring harnesses and connectors. Corrosion, pinched cables, or a cracked connector shell are common culprits.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect and reconnect the cable running from the drive unit to the display. Check for bent pins.

fixSteps.title: Clean contacts
fixSteps.instruction: Use contact cleaner on connector pins and reassemble.

fixSteps.title: Replace harness
fixSteps.instruction: If damage is visible, have the wiring harness replaced at a dealer.

whenToCallPro: If wiring inside the frame is suspected, visit a bike shop.

faq.a: Usually it is a cable issue and can be resolved cheaply.

title: Lighting system error
shortDescription: The bike's lighting circuit has a fault.
fullDescription:
Error 502 is triggered when the lighting system reports an over-current, short circuit, or a broken light cable. The system disables lights to protect the drive unit.

This fault does not stop motor assist on most models but should still be fixed for safety.

fixSteps.title: Inspect lights
fixSteps.instruction: Check headlight and tail light cables for damage or pinching.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect lights
fixSteps.instruction: Temporarily disconnect lights to confirm the error clears.

fixSteps.title: Replace faulty light
fixSteps.instruction: Install a compatible Bosch-approved light unit.

affectedModels: All Bosch eBike systems with integrated lighting
whenToCallPro: If wiring runs inside the frame or you are uncomfortable with electrical work.

faq.a: Yes, but you should not ride at night until lights are fixed.

title: Speed sensor error
shortDescription: The speed sensor signal is missing or invalid.
fullDescription:
Error 503 means the drive unit is not receiving a correct speed sensor signal. This is nearly always due to a misaligned spoke magnet or a damaged sensor on the chainstay.

Motor assist is disabled for safety because the system cannot verify bike speed.

fixSteps.title: Check magnet alignment
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the spoke magnet lines up with the sensor on the chainstay with a 5-8 mm gap.

fixSteps.title: Clean sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the sensor face and magnet of mud and metallic debris.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor or magnet
fixSteps.instruction: If still faulty, replace the spoke magnet or speed sensor.

whenToCallPro: If the sensor cable is routed internally and difficult to replace.

title: Speed sensor manipulation detected
shortDescription: The system detects implausible speed readings, often from tuning devices.
fullDescription:
Error 504 is triggered when the drive unit detects speed readings that do not match expected values, such as those caused by speed-limit tuning dongles.

Remove any tuning device and reset. Note that tuning devices void the warranty and may be illegal on public roads.

fixSteps.title: Remove tuning devices
fixSteps.instruction: Uninstall any aftermarket speed manipulation device.

fixSteps.title: Verify single magnet
fixSteps.instruction: Make sure only the original Bosch magnet is on the wheel.

fixSteps.title: Dealer diagnostic reset
fixSteps.instruction: If error persists, a Bosch dealer may need to reset the stored fault with DiagnosticTool.

whenToCallPro: If a dealer reset is required to clear the stored fault.

faq.a: They are illegal on public roads in most countries and void warranty.

title: Internal sensor error
shortDescription: An internal sensor in the drive unit has failed.
fullDescription:
Error 510 indicates that a sensor inside the drive unit (torque, cadence, or temperature) is giving an implausible reading. This is typically not user-repairable.

A dealer must open or replace the motor unit.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Remove battery and reinstall. Check if error clears.

fixSteps.title: Visit dealer
fixSteps.instruction: Take the bike to a Bosch-certified dealer for diagnostics.

whenToCallPro: Always. This fault requires dealer diagnostics.

faq.a: Often yes, but check warranty status first.

title: Internal drive unit fault
shortDescription: Drive unit reports an unspecified internal fault.
fullDescription:
Error 511 is a generic internal error in the Bosch drive unit. It may appear transiently during firmware issues or permanently following hardware failure.

Power cycle first. Persistent error codes require a dealer visit.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Remove battery for 30 seconds, reinstall and power on.

fixSteps.title: Firmware update
fixSteps.instruction: Have dealer run DiagnosticTool firmware update.

whenToCallPro: If the error persists after reboot.

faq.a: Only if you are comfortable without assist; have it checked soon.

title: Battery error
shortDescription: The battery reports a fault condition.
fullDescription:
Error 530 indicates that the battery BMS (battery management system) has detected a problem such as over-temperature, under-voltage, or internal cell imbalance.

Let the battery rest at room temperature. Charge fully and recheck. Never use a damaged or swollen battery.

causes.cause: Battery too cold or too hot

fixSteps.title: Let battery reach room temperature
fixSteps.instruction: Allow battery to warm to 15-25 C before charging.

fixSteps.title: Full charge cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Charge the battery fully and reinsert on the bike.

fixSteps.title: Battery diagnostic
fixSteps.instruction: If error persists, dealer must run battery diagnostic.

whenToCallPro: If battery is swollen, leaking, or shows physical damage, do NOT charge it. Take to dealer.

faq.a: Yes, it is a fire risk. Store outdoors and contact a dealer.

title: Battery temperature out of range
shortDescription: The battery is too hot or too cold to operate.
fullDescription:
Error 540 appears when the battery temperature is outside the safe operating range (approximately 0-40 C for discharge). The BMS blocks discharge to protect the cells.

Move the bike to a temperate environment and wait. Do not charge a battery that has just come in from freezing conditions.

causes.cause: Battery overheated after riding in the sun

fixSteps.title: Move to moderate temperature
fixSteps.instruction: Bring bike and battery indoors (15-25 C).

fixSteps.title: Wait for stabilization
fixSteps.instruction: Allow the battery to reach safe temperature before use.

fixSteps.title: Retry
fixSteps.instruction: Power on the system and check the error has cleared.

whenToCallPro: Only if the error appears without temperature extremes.

faq.q: Can I store my battery in the garage in winter?

title: Impermissible electrical consumer detected
shortDescription: An unauthorized electrical accessory is connected to the battery.
fullDescription:
Error 550 appears when the system detects a non-approved load, typically an aftermarket USB charger or light that draws current directly from the battery connector.

Remove the unauthorized accessory and power cycle the bike.

fixSteps.title: Remove unauthorized accessories
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect any aftermarket electronics tied directly to the battery.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Remove battery and reinstall.

whenToCallPro: If error returns without any accessory installed.

faq.q: Can I add a USB charger?
faq.a: Only if it is Bosch-approved and uses the correct port.

title: Impermissible battery discharge
shortDescription: The BMS detected an implausible discharge pattern.
fullDescription:
Error 551 is shown when the battery BMS logs an unusual discharge event, such as a sudden high current spike or a short. This can be caused by a faulty load, internal damage, or external parasitic draw.

Disconnect any accessories and perform a full charge cycle. If the error returns, have the battery and drive unit checked.

fixSteps.title: Remove accessories
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect all non-original accessories.

fixSteps.title: Full charge
fixSteps.instruction: Perform a full charge cycle and observe.

fixSteps.title: Dealer diagnostic
fixSteps.instruction: If error returns, have the battery diagnosed.

whenToCallPro: If the error persists or the battery acts abnormally.

faq.a: Not usually, but monitor for heat or swelling.

title: Charger error
shortDescription: The charger is not recognized or has failed.
fullDescription:
Error 560 is reported when the battery cannot communicate with or is not getting the expected voltage from the charger. Non-Bosch chargers frequently trigger this code.

Use only the original Bosch charger. Inspect the charger cable and connector.

fixSteps.title: Use original charger
fixSteps.instruction: Replace third-party charger with genuine Bosch charger.

fixSteps.title: Inspect charger
fixSteps.instruction: Check for visible damage, a broken LED, or a frayed cable.

fixSteps.title: Test another battery
fixSteps.instruction: If available, test the charger on another Bosch battery to isolate the fault.

whenToCallPro: If a known-good charger still produces the error.

faq.a: No, only the approved Bosch charger.

title: Charger not recognized
shortDescription: The charger is incompatible or damaged.
fullDescription:
Error 561 is very similar to 560 but specifically indicates that the battery does not recognize the connected charger's identity signal. Dirty or bent pins in the charge port are common causes.

Inspect the port and use a genuine Bosch charger.

fixSteps.title: Clean charging port
fixSteps.instruction: Use a soft brush and contact cleaner on the battery charge port.

fixSteps.title: Try another charger
fixSteps.instruction: If available, test a known-good genuine Bosch charger.

fixSteps.title: Inspect port pins
fixSteps.instruction: Check for bent or damaged pins. Have port repaired if damaged.

whenToCallPro: If port pins are bent or damaged.

faq.a: Yes, it is the most common cause.

title: Battery internal error during charging
shortDescription: Internal battery fault detected while charging.
fullDescription:
Error 602 is reported by the battery BMS during charging. It is usually a temperature or cell-voltage protection condition. Occasionally appears when the battery is nearly empty and cold.

Let the battery rest at room temperature and retry. Persistent error requires service.

fixSteps.title: Warm battery
fixSteps.instruction: Bring battery to room temperature before charging.

fixSteps.title: Retry charging
fixSteps.instruction: Try charging again once battery is warm.

fixSteps.title: Dealer service
fixSteps.instruction: If error persists, have battery diagnosed.

whenToCallPro: If error persists after warming and retry.

faq.q: Is it safe to keep charging?
faq.a: Only at moderate temperature; stop if the error returns.

title: Battery internal error
shortDescription: Battery reports a persistent internal fault.
fullDescription:
Error 603 is similar to 602 but the fault is persistent and typically not self-clearing. It usually indicates a failed cell or BMS circuit inside the battery pack.

Do not open the battery. Take it to a Bosch dealer for service or replacement.

fixSteps.title: Do not open battery
fixSteps.instruction: Do not attempt DIY repair on lithium-ion packs.

fixSteps.title: Take to dealer
fixSteps.instruction: Dealer will test the pack and offer repair or replacement.

whenToCallPro: Always for this code. Lithium-ion packs are a fire risk if mishandled.

faq.a: Not safely. Replace with an authorized Bosch battery.
